messages:
maya: FYI support flagged a customer p99 spike right after last week's kernel/attention roll (FlashAttention v2 -> v3). Customer: fin-reports-prod. They see p95 ~1.1s -> 2.6s and p99 > 4s for short chat completions.
jess-oncall: ack, can you paste the support thread or repro?
sam-support: pasted logs below. reported at 08:12 UTC. Repro using hosted API -> model redwood-13b-lite. Sample curl and timings: 
```
$ time curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"model":"redwood-13b-lite","input":"summarize: quarterly results"}'
real 0m2.45s
```
Yesterday same request: real 0m1.05s. p99 diverging across many customers.
maya: thanks. we shipped a compile/kernel update that prefers FlashAttention v3 and toggles SDPA path for sequences < 512. suspect kernel selection/regression.
ben-platform: I saw higher tail on nodes in us-west2-gpupool-7 around the deploy window. Kernel build tag: 2026-03-kernel-qat-v3.
ton y-rt: fwiw, perf traces show far more time in attention kernel for short contexts. Call stacks show 30-40% extra time in interleaved CUDA kernels.
azadeh: @maya can you share the exact env/flags used? maybe a compile flag changed numeric precision or vectorization?
maya: build flags: `-DFLASH_ATTENTION=1 -DUSE_SDPA_AUTO=1 -O3 -march=sm80 -DFP16_KV=true`. Previously we had `-DUSE_SDPA_AUTO=0`.
jess-oncall: immediate mitigation request from support: can we flip SDPA back to 0 per-customer or per-node? customer is blocking.
ben-platform: we can set an env var so runtime prefers SDPA=0: `REDWOOD_USE_SDPA=0` but need a node restart for kernel reload. alternative: set runtime kernel selector override to prefer legacy SDPA path.
maya: quick repro on local with same model: toggling SDPA off drops median & tails back to baseline. Repro steps: 
1) checkout commit 8f3a
2) build runtime with env `REDWOOD_USE_SDPA=1` vs `0`
3) run `./inference_server --model redwood-13b-lite --port 8080`
4) `ab -n 50 -c 5 http://localhost:8080/generate` -> see p99 delta.
```
SDPA=1 p99: 4200ms
SDPA=0 p99: 980ms
```

maya: given that, propose two-step mitigation: 1) hotpatch prod node pool to set `REDWOOD_USE_SDPA=0` for affected pools (us-west2-gpupool-7), 2) pin kernel selection to older kernel (2026-02-kernel-qat-v2) as fallback if hotpatch insufficient.

jen s-oncall: is there any functional correctness risk? will outputs differ?
maya: no significant quality change based on our metric sampling (ROUGE/BERTscore) across 200 sample prompts. differences <0.5%. good to toggle for latency SLO.
ben-platform: plan for deploy: create new node image with env var set and drain/replace 20% at a time. ETA ~35-40m to start seeing effect.
ton y-rt: we should also add a kernel selector flag at request time: `kernel_preference=legacy_sdpa` so we can route single customer to safe kernel with no node restart. But that needs console + routing update.
azadeh: can we do a per-customer routing override quickly? I can hack a rule in routing layer to send fin-reports-prod to us-west2-oldkernel pool.
sam-support: customer asked for ETA and temporary workaround. They can also try lowering `max_tokens` but that's not ideal.
infra-bot: Incident note created: INC-2026-0442 — p99 regression after attention kernel update. Link: https://incidents.redwood/INC-2026-0442
maya: I'm going to flip SDPA off on a small canary subset (2 nodes) and run benchmarks. will post numbers.
(15m later)
maya: Canary results: SDPA=0 nodes saw p99 drop from 4.2s -> 0.95s for same load. CPU/GPU utilization similar or slightly lower. Looks good.
ben-platform: starting rolling patch: new node image with REDWOOD_USE_SDPA=0, draining 5 nodes and replacing. Rolling target 20% every 10m.
sam-support: customer updated: appreciated and will monitor. asked for notification when resolved for all regions.
(40m later)
deploy-bot: Rollout started by ben-platform for image redwood-node-2026-03-sdpa-off (5/25 updated).
(1h later)
maya: after 25% rolled, global p99 across redwood-13b-lite traffic down ~60% from peak. us-west2 p99 back to ~1s.
tony-rt: we should also track any regression on long sequences (>1024) where SDPA had benefits. run battery tests.
azadeh: running long sequence perf test on both kernels: SDPA=1 still better for >2048 sequences by ~15% throughput. we'll need a smarter kernel selector based on seq length.
maya: bug hypothesis: SDPA selector heuristic used sequence length cutoff 512 but new FlashAttention kernels had slower small-seq performance due to additional indexing overhead. selector should prefer legacy for seq < 768 for this model family.
\en vir-bot: Perf job scheduled: perf-job-23678905 for redwood-13b-lite comparing kernel v2/v3 across seq lengths [16,64,256,512,1024,2048]. Results ETA 2h.
ben-platform: next steps: 1) complete rollback of SDPA default to 0 until we ship selector tweak 2) add kernel_selection_override parameter in console for per-route control 3) run full canary and QA for kernel v3 with selector heuristics adjusted.
jess-oncall: do we want to keep node image with SDPA=0 as long-term?
maya: not long-term. we want to re-enable v3 once selector fixed. but keep the per-node image in case of future regressions.
sam-support: customer confirms p99 back to baseline. closing their escalation, they want postmortem.
maya: I'll draft a short postmortem and include timelines, root cause (SDPA heuristic + FA v3 overhead), mitigation (hotpatch + selector change), and next actions.
ben-platform: assign owners: maya -> root cause + selector fix, azadeh -> routing override and console param, tony-rt -> perf validation and kernel tuning, jess-oncall -> finalize incident ticket and comms.
maya: thanks team. important note: add a perf check in CI to compare p99 before promoting kernel changes to prod. a simple perf gate for short-context workloads.
zendesk-bot: Support ticket #7412 updated: status -> resolved.
maya: closing thread once postmortem posted. :thumbsup:
